newsitem.title: BELARUS: World Bank sees $200 mln/yr to Belarus if reforms.
newsitem.headline: World Bank sees $200 mln/yr to Belarus if reforms.

text.p: The World Bank could issue the former Soviet republic of Belarus credits totalling $200 million a year if it fulfilled conditions for economic reform, the World Bank country resident said on Wednesday.

Christopher Willoughby, completing four years as head of the World Bank's Belarus office, said in a statement the bank was hopeful Belarus would make more effort to reform following the signing of a memorandum of understanding earlier this month.
The World Bank has not issued new loans to Belarus in three years though Belarus has received a total of $170 million from the Bank since the Soviet Union fell apart in 1991.
The memorandum calls for Belarus to liberalise prices and the currency market, create a climate friendly to business, and limit government interference in the banking sector.
But Willoughby said on Tuesday that reforms had reversed, state interference had grown, and the economy could take 10 years to recover.
